chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Ibn Abi Yafur, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Bazi'a claims that he is a prophet.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'So if you hear him saying that, kill him.' He (the narrator) said, 'I sat [waiting] more than once, but I was not able to do that.'

key_terms.بَزِيعاً: Bazi'a, a specific historical figure known for claiming prophethood

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling for someone who claims to be a prophet?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the specific hadd penalty for a self-proclaimed prophet, emphasizing the necessity of hearing the explicit claim to execute the ruling. The narrator’s repeated waiting highlights the scholarly caution required to distinguish between a definitive claim and mere assertion, ensuring the penalty is applied only upon clear evidence. This ruling is distinct from general apostasy, focusing specifically on the novelty of the prophetic claim within the Islamic framework.
